title: An amygdala to anterior hypothalamic circuit gates stress sensitivity.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: no PMCID, no Europe PMC full text, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI links (GEO/SRA/BioProject). Crossref shows CC-BY 4.0 licence. Zenodo search (topic and author Pennington), Figshare search, DANDI (DANDI, a neurophysiology data archive) search and GitHub search all returned nothing for this study. nature.com page redirects to a login/cookie wall; bioRxiv preprint (10.1101/2024.10.28.620614) XML returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited); preprint not in Europe PMC full text.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the data comes from the abstract: whole-brain c-Fos (an activity marker gene) mapping in previously stressed vs naive mice, Miniscope (head-mounted microscope) calcium imaging of AHN (anterior hypothalamic nucleus) neurons, chemogenetic/optogenetic manipulations. No mouse counts, neuron counts or data availability statement were seen.

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited dataset found in Zenodo, Figshare, DANDI, GitHub, GEO or Europe PMC; data availability statement not retrievable (paywall redirect, preprint rate-limited). Checked repositories, not the paper's statement; Nature source data spreadsheets may exist but would be per-figure summaries.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked in files. Labels would be group (stressed vs naive) or stimulus valence per imaging frame; any per-figure source data would hold group means or per-animal summaries, not a model-ready table.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked; raw Miniscope videos or cell-by-time traces were not found anywhere.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not verified. In a circuit-neuroscience study of this type the independent unit is the mouse, typically tens per group, far below the ~400 rows needed even for classification; neuron counts could be in the hundreds but are nested within few animals.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Processed c-Fos region counts or extracted calcium traces would be small; raw whole-brain light-sheet images would not. Not verified.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No files to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would be experimental conditions (stress history, shock/stimulus delivery), physical measurements rather than model outputs. From abstract only.

backbone.name: none applicable (no open-weight foundation model for c-Fos region counts; neural-population models like POYO/NDT need large spiking/imaging corpora)

integration.partner_dataset: Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas (region-to-region projection strengths), joinable on Allen CCF (Common Coordinate Framework) region acronyms if region-level c-Fos counts were released
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does anatomical connectivity predict which regions become co-activated with the AHN after prior stress? Moot without released region counts.

controls.positive_control: Would be: stressed vs naive classification recovering AHN and amygdala as top features, as the paper reports.
controls.negative_control: Would be: shuffle group labels across mice.
controls.external_validation: Other public whole-brain c-Fos stress datasets (e.g. Lab Animal / serial two-photon studies) exist but none retrieved with data.

honest_claim_h3: At best: distinguishes previously stressed from naive mice by whole-brain c-Fos pattern within one lab's cohort of a few dozen mice, which the paper already shows with simple statistics.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use brain-wide activity-marker counts or hypothalamic neuron activity to predict whether a mouse has prior stress history or stimulus valence.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-mouse counts of c-Fos-positive (recently active) cells across brain regions, or per-neuron calcium activity traces from AHN; number of mice or neurons unknown (not seen).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the mouse was previously stressed (set by the experimenters) or whether a stimulus was aversive, as recorded in the experimental design.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Could tell stress neuroscientists whether a brain-wide activity signature of stress history generalises; but with no released data and few animals it cannot be done here.

ml_idea: Classify stress history from whole-brain c-Fos region counts, or decode stimulus valence from AHN Miniscope traces, with leave-one-mouse-out evaluation. Not feasible: no deposited data found and the unit (mouse) is far too few.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; no data files were located.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the Nature data availability statement: if it says 'available on request' or only per-figure source data, the project is dead.

verdict_reason: A1/A5 failure: a paywalled Nature circuit-neuroscience paper with no data found in any public repository (Zenodo, Figshare, DANDI, GitHub, GEO), data statement unreadable, and the independent unit is the mouse, likely tens per group, well under any ML threshold.
